profile.reading:
This point is mapped as NTT's VA8 building, with an OSM geocoded address in the 44700 block of Gigabit Plaza in Ashburn, Virginia, on the same Gigabit Plaza street as NTT's confirmed VA3, VA6, VA7, and VA9 buildings nearby. NTT's own Ashburn campus overview page names and links only seven buildings today, VA1, VA2, VA3, VA4, VA5, VA7, and VA11. VA8 does not appear anywhere in that list or elsewhere on NTT's public site, even though the street address for this entry comes from public geocoded property records placing a real structure at this location. Because NTT has not published a dedicated facility page for VA8, this entry does not assert a square footage or a megawatt figure for the building specifically, since none exists in NTT's own public materials to confirm.

NTT describes its overall Ashburn campus, as a whole, as delivering 224 megawatts of critical IT load across 78 acres in Loudoun County's Data Center Alley. That combined figure necessarily includes whatever capacity VA8 itself contributes, but NTT does not break the total out building by building for every address on the campus, so this entry cannot state VA8's individual share of that 224 megawatt figure. NTT's own numbering on this campus runs at least through VA11, the highest building number NTT names on its own site, though gaps in that sequence, including VA6, VA8, and VA9, currently have no individually published facility page despite carrying real, numbered addresses on the same streets NTT does document.

NTT's individually documented buildings on this campus offer a rough scale reference for what a typical building here looks like, though not a confirmed match for VA8. VA1, a short distance away at 44664 Guilford Drive, is confirmed on NTT's own site at 64,723 square feet of raised floor and 12.6 megawatts of critical IT load. This entry does not apply VA1's specific numbers to VA8, since NTT has never confirmed the two buildings are comparable in size or design, and building footprints visibly vary across this campus.

Virginia's data center growth is also reshaping statewide electricity rates in ways that reach every building on this campus. In November 2026, the Virginia State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates that raise a typical residential bill by about 16 dollars a month, to roughly 165 dollars, while creating a new GS-5 rate class specifically for data centers, effective January 1, 2027. Large demand campus buildings like this one face 14 year mandatory minimum contracts and cost coverage requirements under that new class, according to Inside Climate News's reporting on the commission's decision. That regulatory shift applies to the campus and to VA8's undocumented capacity alike, even though this entry cannot say how large a share of the 224 megawatt campus total VA8 itself represents.

sources.title: Virginia regulators approve new Dominion Energy rates, data center rate class

reading.body:
VA8 is a building on NTT's Ashburn campus in Loudoun County, Virginia, but NTT has not published individual specifications for it. The campus as a whole delivers 224 megawatts of critical IT load across 78 acres, and VA8 contributes an unknown share of that total. NTT's own documentation names only seven of at least eleven buildings on this campus, leaving VA8 and several other numbered addresses without published facility pages, though the building exists at a geocoded address on Gigabit Plaza.

Without a published breakdown by building, this entry cannot state VA8's capacity or size. A comparable building nearby, VA1, holds 12.6 megawatts in 64,723 square feet, but NTT has never confirmed that VA8 matches that footprint or design. At an industry assumption of 40 kilowatts per rack in AI training density, a building equivalent to VA1 would house roughly 315 racks, but that figure does not apply to VA8 unless NTT confirms the buildings are similar.

Virginia's Dominion Energy rate class for data centers, effective January 1, 2027, imposes 14-year minimum contracts on large campuses, affecting this building's operating costs regardless of its undisclosed size. The Ashburn campus ranks 26th among all published data center capacity figures in Virginia, a state holding 1603.4 megawatts of mapped capacity across 330 facilities, with only 25 publishing megawatt figures. VA8's role in Virginia's electricity constraint remains unknowable without disclosure.
